code.originalText: Review after eight weeks of pacing and physical therapy; first zoledronic acid infusion; planning endoscopy after heartburn returned off omeprazole

text.paragraph: Review after eight weeks of pacing and physical therapy; zoledronic acid infusion; heartburn back off omeprazole. [S]

Ms. Lange has had seven weeks of physical therapy, two sessions a week of submaximal strengthening and warm-water exercise with rest days. Her right ankle-foot orthosis was fitted four weeks ago and she uses a cane outdoors. She has had no falls. She now plans each field day with rest breaks and a seat stick, has a colleague carry the tripod, and rests the day after; she is less tired and the evening aching is less. Home overnight oximetry six weeks ago was normal. She completed the eight-week omeprazole trial two weeks ago and stopped it; within five days the heartburn and regurgitation came back on three or four nights a week. She has no difficulty swallowing, weight loss, vomiting, or black stools. She has taken vitamin D3 daily, saw her dentist last month with no problems, and has not yet returned the 24-hour urine collection: she was away photographing for two weeks. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1957-04-20; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; walks in with the orthosis and a cane
Strength unchanged from the baseline: left quadriceps 4/5, right quadriceps 3+/5, right ankle dorsiflexion 2/5
With the orthosis, no foot drop and less knee hyperextension; Timed Up and Go 11.8 seconds with the orthosis and cane
No pressure marks from the orthosis
Soft; mild epigastric tenderness; healed upper abdominal scar
Teeth and gums in good repair

New fatigue and slowly increasing weakness for about 18 months, in the left leg and both arms as well as the right leg weakened by polio at seven, with aching muscle pain after work and cold intolerance of the right leg; cause to be established
S — Synthetic presenting concern at the index visit, superseded by the diagnosis of post-polio syndrome at the second visit; the paralytic polio of 1902 is documented (D).

Post-polio syndrome (modified March of Dimes criteria met): new weakness of the left quadriceps and both shoulder girdles and increased weakness of the right leg, with fatigue, muscle pain, and cold intolerance, more than 50 years after paralytic polio with partial recovery and decades of stable function; nerve conduction normal; EMG chronic reinnervation in both legs and the right deltoid; other causes excluded

S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the childhood polio is documented (D), and her biographer's account of post-polio symptoms later in life is a retrospective interpretation (R). No neurological finding from her lifetime is used.
Heartburn and regurgitation after meals and at night for three months, three to four times a week; no difficulty swallowing, weight loss, vomiting, bleeding, or anemia
S — Synthetic presenting symptom at the index visit, superseded by the endoscopic diagnosis at the fourth visit.

Osteoporosis, worst at the right hip on the polio-weakened side (right femoral neck T-score -2.7; left -1.6; lumbar spine -1.8), with vitamin D insufficiency; no vertebral fracture on assessment; 10-year FRAX risk about 16 percent major osteoporotic and 4.5 percent hip
S — Synthetic bone density result; disuse of a polio-affected limb lowers bone density on that side.
Two falls in the past year without injury, from catching the right foot
S — Synthetic fall history at presentation.
Surgery for severe stomach ulcers in her early fifties; no ulcer symptoms since; avoids nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
S — Synthetic modern history entry linked to the documented ulcers and surgery of the late 1940s (D); the type of operation is not known.

Post-polio syndrome (G14). Fatigue and pain improving with pacing and non-fatiguing exercise; strength stable; no falls since the orthosis. Pain 5 of 10, from 6. [S]
Finish the twelve weeks of physical therapy, then a home program.
Continue the field-day pacing plan.

Osteoporosis (M81.8). Vitamin D 34 ng/mL, calcium 9.4, creatinine 0.7, eGFR 93; dental check normal. Ready for zoledronic acid. The 24-hour urine calcium was not collected; with normal serum calcium, PTH, and phosphate the infusion goes ahead. [S]
Zoledronic acid 5 mg intravenously today.
She may have fever and aching for a day or two after the first dose; acetaminophen if so.
Urine collection rebooked.

Heartburn that returned after stopping omeprazole (R12). Typical reflux symptoms that responded to omeprazole and returned within days of stopping it. Before committing her to long-term acid suppression, and with an earlier ulcer operation, an upper endoscopy off the proton pump inhibitor will establish the diagnosis and look for esophagitis and Barrett's esophagus. [S]
Upper endoscopy in about ten days, three to four weeks after the last omeprazole dose.
Calcium carbonate chewable tablets as needed until then.
Sedation precautions sent to the endoscopy unit.
